Keywords: JWT bearer token PyJWT access token decode verify InvalidTokenError
Description: Issue signed JWT access tokens on login and verify them on protected routes via a reusable dependency. Uses PyJWT (the library FastAPI docs now recommend). Raises InvalidTokenError on tampered or expired tokens.
When to Use: Stateless APIs where you want no server-side session storage
Code Example:
import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidTokenError
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='/token')
SECRET_KEY = 'your-secret-key'  # openssl rand -hex 32
ALGORITHM = 'HS256'

async def get_current_user(token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)]):
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        username = payload.get('sub')
        if username is None:
            raise HTTPException(401)
    except InvalidTokenError:
        raise HTTPException(401, headers={'WWW-Authenticate': 'Bearer'})
    return username
Security Notes: Use `openssl rand -hex 32` to generate SECRET_KEY. Store in env vars only. Use short ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (e.g. 30). Import InvalidTokenError — not JWTError (that was python-jose).

Keywords: password hash argon2 pwdlib PasswordHash verify recommended
Description: Use pwdlib (FastAPI's currently recommended library) with Argon2 — the recommended hashing algorithm. Replace passlib/bcrypt patterns with pwdlib's PasswordHash.recommended().
When to Use: Any endpoint that stores or checks user passwords
Security Notes: Always call verify_password with DUMMY_HASH when user not found — prevents timing attacks that reveal valid usernames. Argon2 is memory-hard and resistant to GPU attacks.

Keywords: api key x-api-key header APIKeyHeader Security simple machine to machine
Description: Validate a pre-shared API key sent in a request header (X-API-Key) using FastAPI's APIKeyHeader security utility.
When to Use: Service-to-service APIs or webhook consumers without user accounts
Code Example:
from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader
from fastapi import Security
import hmac

api_key_header = APIKeyHeader(name='X-API-Key')

async def verify_api_key(api_key: str = Security(api_key_header)):
    if not hmac.compare_digest(api_key.encode(), settings.API_KEY.encode()):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='Invalid API key')
    return api_key

@router.get('/data', dependencies=[Depends(verify_api_key)])
async def get_data(): ...
Security Notes: Use hmac.compare_digest (constant-time) — never plain == comparison. Rotate keys on any suspected compromise. Store keys in env vars.

Keywords: basic auth HTTPBasic HTTPBasicCredentials username password simple internal
Description: Use FastAPI's HTTPBasic security class. Requires `secrets.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.
When to Use: Admin panels simple internal tools or webhook endpoints with a single shared credential
Code Example:
import secrets
from fastapi.security import HTTPBasic, HTTPBasicCredentials

security = HTTPBasic()

async def verify(creds: Annotated[HTTPBasicCredentials, Depends(security)]):
    correct_user = secrets.compare_digest(creds.username.encode(), b'admin')
    correct_pass = secrets.compare_digest(creds.password.encode(), b'secret')
    if not (correct_user and correct_pass):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=401,
            detail='Incorrect credentials',
            headers={'WWW-Authenticate': 'Basic'},
        )
    return creds.username
Security Notes: Always check both username AND password before rejecting (prevents username enumeration). Use secrets.compare_digest — not == or != operators.

Keywords: Annotated dependency alias reuse type hint clean DRY injection
Description: Use Annotated to create a reusable type alias for a dependency. Avoids repeating Depends(...) on every route and makes signatures cleaner.
When to Use: When the same dependency is used across many routes and you want DRY code
Code Example:
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends

# Define once
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_active_user)]
DbSession = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]

# Use everywhere cleanly
@router.get('/me')
async def read_me(user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession):
    ...

@router.put('/me')
async def update_me(user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession, body: UserUpdate):
    ...
Security Notes: This is the FastAPI-recommended pattern for sharing dependencies across many routes. Documented in FastAPI official tutorial as 'Share Annotated dependencies'.
